# dhseqr

> Computes the eigenvalues of a Hessenberg matrix H and, optionally, the matrices T and Z from the Schur decomposition H = Z T Zᵀ.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dhseqr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dhseqr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dhseqr(
    order,
    job, compz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    H, LDH,
    WR, strideWR,
    WI, strideWI,
    Z, LDZ,
    work
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `job` | `("eigenvalues"\|"schur")` | in |  | one of `'eigenvalues'`, `'schur'` | `'eigenvalues'`: compute eigenvalues only; `'schur'`: compute eigenvalues and the Schur form T. |
| `compz` | `("none"\|"initialize"\|"update")` | in |  | one of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'` | `'none'`: no Schur vectors are computed; `'initialize'`: Z is initialized to the unit matrix and the matrix Z of Schur vectors of H is returned; `'update'`: Z must contain an orthogonal matrix Q on entry, and the product Q*Z is returned. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | the order of the matrix H. |
| `ilo` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )` | it is assumed that H is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:ILO-1 and IHI+1:N. |
| `ihi` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N` | it is assumed that H is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:ILO-1 and IHI+1:N. |
| `H` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | on entry, the upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if INFO = 0 and `job === 'schur'`, then H contains the upper quasi-triangular matrix T from the Schur decomposition (the Schur form); 2-by-2 diagonal blocks (corresponding to complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues) are returned in standard form, with H(i,i) = H(i+1,i+1) and H(i+1,i)*H(i,i+1) < 0. |
| ↳ `LDH` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | requires `LDH ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `H` |
| `WR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WR` |
| `WI` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WI` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | if `compz === 'none'`, Z is not referenced. |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| ((compz === 'initialize' \|\| compz === 'update') && ldz < max( 1, N ))` | leading dimension of `Z` |
| `work` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, N )` |  | workspace of at least `max(1,N)` elements (the reference's minimum), or `null` to allocate the reference's optimum (`max( max(1,N), LWKOPT of DLAQR0 )`) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `job`:

  -   `= 'E'`: compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'S'`: compute eigenvalues and the Schur form T.
- `compz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: no Schur vectors are computed;
  -   `= 'I'`: Z is initialized to the unit matrix and the matrix Z of Schur vectors of H is returned;
  -   `= 'V'`: Z must contain an orthogonal matrix Q on entry, and the product $Q \, Z$ is returned.
- `N`: The order of the matrix H. $N \ge 0$.
- `ihi`: It is assumed that H is already upper triangular in rows and columns 1:`ILO`-1 and `IHI`+1:N. `ILO` and `IHI` are normally set by a previous call to DGEBAL, and then passed to ZGEHRD when the matrix output by DGEBAL is reduced to Hessenberg form. Otherwise `ILO` and `IHI` should be set to 1 and N respectively. If $N > 0$, then $1 \le \mathrm{ILO} \le \mathrm{IHI} \le N$. If $N = 0$, then `ILO = 1` and `IHI = 0`.
- `H`: On entry, the upper Hessenberg matrix H. On exit, if `INFO = 0` and `JOB = 'S'`, then H contains the upper quasi-triangular matrix T from the Schur decomposition (the Schur form); 2-by-2 diagonal blocks (corresponding to complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues) are returned in standard form, with $H(i,i) = H(i+1,i+1)$ and $H(i+1,i) \, H(i,i+1) < 0$. If `INFO = 0` and `JOB = 'E'`, the contents of H are unspecified on exit. (The output value of H when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)

  Unlike earlier versions of DHSEQR, this subroutine may explicitly $H(i,j) = 0$ for $i > j$ and $j = 1$, 2, ... `ILO`-1 or $j = \mathrm{IHI}+1$, `IHI`+2, ... N.
- `WI`: The real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. If two eigenvalues are computed as a complex conjugate pair, they are stored in consecutive elements of `WR` and `WI`, say the i-th and (i+1)th, with $\mathrm{WI}(i) > 0$ and $\mathrm{WI}(i+1) < 0$. If `JOB = 'S'`, the eigenvalues are stored in the same order as on the diagonal of the Schur form returned in H, with `WR(i) = H(i,i)` and, if `H(i:i+1,i:i+1)` is a 2-by-2 diagonal block, `WI(i) = sqrt(-H(i+1,i)*H(i,i+1))` and `WI(i+1) = -WI(i)`.
- `Z`: If `COMPZ = 'N'`, Z is not referenced. If `COMPZ = 'I'`, on entry Z need not be set and on exit, if `INFO = 0`, Z contains the orthogonal matrix Z of the Schur vectors of H. If `COMPZ = 'V'`, on entry Z must contain an N-by-N matrix Q, which is assumed to be equal to the unit matrix except for the submatrix `Z(ILO:IHI,ILO:IHI)`. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, Z contains $Q \, Z$. Normally Q is the orthogonal matrix generated by DORGHR after the call to DGEHRD which formed the Hessenberg matrix H. (The output value of Z when $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ is given under the description of `INFO` below.)
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns an estimate of the optimal value for `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "eigenvalues", "schur"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )`)
- `RangeError` sixth argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( ( compz === "initialize" \|\| compz === "update" ) && LDZ < max( 1, N ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dhseqr.ndarray(
    job, compz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi,
    H, strideH1, strideH2, offsetH,
    WR, strideWR, offsetWR,
    WI, strideWI, offsetWI,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    work, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Computes the eigenvalues of a real upper Hessenberg matrix H, and.
optionally the matrices T and Z from the Schur decomposition
H = Z _ T _ Z**T, where T is an upper quasi-triangular matrix (the
Schur form) and Z is the orthogonal matrix of Schur vectors.

JOB = 'E': compute eigenvalues only.
JOB = 'S': compute eigenvalues and the Schur form T.

COMPZ = 'N': no Schur vectors are computed.
COMPZ = 'I': Z is initialized to the identity matrix and the matrix Z
             of Schur vectors of H is returned.
COMPZ = 'V': Z must contain an orthogonal matrix Q on entry, and the
             product Q*Z is returned.

ILO and IHI are 1-based indices (Fortran convention). The active block
is H(ILO:IHI, ILO:IHI). Elements outside this block are assumed already
upper triangular. Normally ILO=1 and IHI=N.

On exit, if INFO = 0, WR and WI contain the real and imaginary parts
of the computed eigenvalues. Complex eigenvalues occur in conjugate
pairs in consecutive entries. If JOB = 'S', the eigenvalues are stored
in the same order as on the diagonal of T.

INFO = 0: success.
INFO > 0: dhseqr failed to compute all eigenvalues. Elements
          INFO+1:IHI of WR and WI contain those eigenvalues which
          have been successfully computed.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job` | `("eigenvalues"\|"schur")` | in |  | one of `'eigenvalues'`, `'schur'` | `'eigenvalues'` or `'schur'` |
| `compz` | `("none"\|"initialize"\|"update")` | in |  | one of `'initialize'`, `'none'`, `'update'` | `'none'`, `'initialize'`, or `'update'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix H |
| `ilo` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )` | first row/col of the active block (1-based) |
| `ihi` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N` | last row/col of the active block (1-based) |
| `H` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | upper Hessenberg matrix (N-by-N) |
| ↳ `strideH1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `strideH2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `offsetH` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `H` |
| `WR` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for real parts of eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WR` |
| ↳ `offsetWR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WR` |
| `WI` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for imaginary parts of eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideWI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `WI` |
| ↳ `offsetWI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WI` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | Schur vectors matrix (N-by-N) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `Z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Z` |
| `work` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ max( 1, N )` |  | workspace array of at least `max(1,N)` elements from `offsetWork` (the reference's minimum); the reference's optimum is `max( max(1,N), LWKOPT of DLAQR0 )` |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `work` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `work` |

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, >0 if failed to converge

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "eigenvalues", "schur"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "initialize", "none", "update"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument is invalid (rejected when `ilo < 1 \|\| ilo > max( 1, N )`)
- `RangeError` fifth argument is invalid (rejected when `ihi < min( ilo, N ) \|\| ihi > N`)
- `RangeError` work array must be large enough

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, DHSEQR failed to compute all of the eigenvalues.  Elements 1:ilo-1 and i+1:n of `WR` and `WI` contain those eigenvalues which have been successfully computed.  (Failures are rare.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `JOB = 'E'`, then on exit, the remaining unconverged eigenvalues are the eigen- values of the upper Hessenberg matrix rows and columns `ILO` through `INFO` of the final, output value of H.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `JOB = 'S'`, then on exit

```text
(*)  (initial value of H)*U  = U*(final value of H)
```

where U is an orthogonal matrix. The final value of H is upper Hessenberg and quasi-triangular in rows and columns `INFO`+1 through `IHI`.

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'V'`, then on exit

(final value of Z) = (initial value of Z)\*U

where U is the orthogonal matrix in (\*) (regard- less of the value of `JOB`.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'I'`, then on exit

(final value of Z) = U

where U is the orthogonal matrix in (\*) (regard- less of the value of `JOB`.)

If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$ and `COMPZ = 'N'`, then Z is not accessed.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dhseqr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dhseqr';

const N = 3;

// 3x3 upper Hessenberg matrix H (column-major):
const Hvals = [ 4.0, 1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 3.0, 0.5, -1.0, 1.0, 2.0 ];

// Note: `ilo` and `ihi` are 1-based for this routine.

// Using the standard interface:
let H = new Float64Array( Hvals );
let WR = new Float64Array( N );
let WI = new Float64Array( N );
let Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
let info = dhseqr( 'column-major', 'schur', 'initialize', N, 1, N, H, N, WR, 1, WI, 1, Z, N, null );
console.log( info );
console.log( WR, WI );

// Using the ndarray interface:
H = new Float64Array( Hvals );
WR = new Float64Array( N );
WI = new Float64Array( N );
Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( N );
info = dhseqr.ndarray( 'schur', 'initialize', N, 1, N, H, 1, N, 0, WR, 1, 0, WI, 1, 0, Z, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info );
console.log( WR, WI );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DHSEQR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DHSEQR computes the eigenvalues of a Hessenberg matrix H and, optionally, the matrices T and Z from the Schur decomposition $H = Z$ T $Z^T$, where T is an upper quasi-triangular matrix (the Schur form), and Z is the orthogonal matrix of Schur vectors.

Optionally Z may be postmultiplied into an input orthogonal matrix Q so that this routine can give the Schur factorization of a matrix A which has been reduced to the Hessenberg form H by the orthogonal matrix Q: $A = Q \, H \, Q^T = (\mathrm{QZ}) \, T \, (\mathrm{QZ})^T$.

### Further Details

Default values supplied by ILAENV(ISPEC,'DHSEQR',`JOB(:1)`//`COMPZ(:1)`,N,`ILO`,`IHI`,`LWORK`). It is suggested that these defaults be adjusted in order to attain best performance in each particular computational environment.

$\mathrm{ISPEC}=12$: The DLAHQR vs DLAQR0 crossover point.

Default: 75. (Must be at least 11.)

$\mathrm{ISPEC}=13$: Recommended deflation window size.

-   This depends on `ILO`, `IHI` and NS. NS is the
-   number of simultaneous shifts returned
-   by ILAENV(ISPEC=15). (See $\mathrm{ISPEC}=15$ below.)
-   The default for $(\mathrm{IHI}-\mathrm{ILO}+1) \le 500$ is NS.
-   The default for $(\mathrm{IHI}-\mathrm{ILO}+1) > 500$ is $3 \, \mathrm{NS}/2$.

$\mathrm{ISPEC}=14$: Nibble crossover point. (See IPARMQ for

-   details.) Default: 14% of deflation window
-   size.

$\mathrm{ISPEC}=15$: Number of simultaneous shifts in a multishift

QR iteration.

$$
\mathrm{If} \mathrm{IHI}-\mathrm{ILO}+1 \mathrm{is} ..
$$

| greater than | ...but less | ... the |
| --- | --- | --- |
| or equal to ... | than | default is |

```text
   1               30          NS =   2(+)
  30               60          NS =   4(+)
  60              150          NS =  10(+)
 150              590          NS =  **
 590             3000          NS =  64
3000             6000          NS = 128
6000             infinity      NS = 256
```

(+) By default some or all matrices of this order

-   are passed to the implicit double shift routine
-   DLAHQR and this parameter is ignored. See
-   $\mathrm{ISPEC}=12$ above and comments in IPARMQ for
-   details.

$( \, \, )$ The asterisks $( \, \, )$ indicate an ad-hoc

function of N increasing from 10 to 64.

$\mathrm{ISPEC}=16$: Select structured matrix multiply.

-   If the number of simultaneous shifts (specified
-   by $\mathrm{ISPEC}=15$) is less than 14, then the default
-   for $\mathrm{ISPEC}=16$ is 0. Otherwise the default for
-   $\mathrm{ISPEC}=16$ is 2.

### References

K. Braman, R. Byers and R. Mathias, The Multi-Shift QR Algorithm Part I: Maintaining Well Focused Shifts, and Level 3 Performance, SIAM Journal of Matrix Analysis, volume 23, pages 929--947, 2002.

</section>
